X.note: Tilted matted portrait on a dark textured background, with a warm red painting that gives good contrast and focus. The caption bar overlaps the bottom of the mat, and the mat shows through the gradient so the text sits on a mixed backdrop. The headline is large and legible. The credit line is small, grey and low-contrast, so it will be hard to read on a phone. There is a big gap between the two caption lines.

Y.note: The same layout with a sepia archival photo. The subject is small and a long way from the camera, and the photo is low-contrast and washed out. The torn emulsion edge on the right adds some authenticity. The caption bar cuts into the lower part of the photo and mat. The headline is clear and says who the man is and when the photo was taken. The credit line is small and dim, and there is the same wide gap between the two caption lines.

why: X's saturated, close-cropped portrait fills the frame and reads instantly on a small screen, while Y's small, washed-out figure is weaker, even though the layout and caption treatment are almost identical.
top_fix_for_weaker: Crop or zoom in on Hoover so he fills the frame, and boost the photo's contrast. Move the caption below the mat so it doesn't overlap the image. Raise the credit line to at least the headline's brightness at a larger size, and tighten the gap between the two caption lines.
